Product Overview

How SignalForge works

SignalForge is a lightweight observability layer for API reliability. It sits outside your stack, runs scheduled checks, and routes structured signals to wherever your team responds to them.

Architecture

SignalForge's architecture is deliberately minimal. There are no agents to deploy inside your infrastructure — only your configured monitors polling from our edge network, emitting signals when thresholds are crossed.

SignalForge polls your endpoints from a distributed edge network. You define what to check, how often, and what constitutes failure. The engine handles scheduling, deduplication, and routing — your infrastructure only sees inbound HTTP probes.

Core concepts

Concept 01
Signal

A typed observation emitted when a monitor check completes. A signal carries a type (e.g. status_not_2xx), a measured value, the configured threshold, severity, and metadata about the environment. Signals are the primitive unit in SignalForge.

Concept 02
Monitor

A scheduled check definition. Monitors specify what to probe (HTTP endpoint, TCP port, or custom Lua probe), how often, and how to validate the response (status code, body regex, latency threshold). Defined in YAML and synced via CLI.

Concept 03
Alert Rule

A composable condition that determines when a signal triggers a notification. Rules support AND/OR logic across multiple signal types, consecutive-failure thresholds, and scheduled maintenance windows. Attach multiple destinations per rule.

Concept 04
Webhook

SignalForge can deliver signal payloads to any HTTPS endpoint via HTTP POST. Webhook payloads are signed with HMAC-SHA256. Use webhooks to integrate with Slack apps, custom dashboards, or your own incident management system.

Monitor types

Type Description Signal types emitted
http HTTP/HTTPS endpoint check. Validates status code, response body, and latency. status_not_2xx, latency_p95_exceeded, body_mismatch
tcp TCP port reachability and connection time check. tcp_timeout, connection_refused
ssl TLS certificate validity and expiry check. cert_expiry_warning, cert_expiry_critical, cert_invalid
dns DNS resolution check. Validates record type, value, and TTL. dns_resolution_failed, dns_value_mismatch

Signal lifecycle

Every signal moves through a defined lifecycle. Understanding this model helps you write accurate alert rules and build reliable integrations.

StateDescriptionTriggers notification?
firing Threshold crossed. Signal is active and unacknowledged. Yes — on first transition
acknowledged An operator has acknowledged the alert. Suppresses repeat notifications. No (unless re-escalation configured)
resolved Monitor returned to healthy state. Recovery signal emitted. Yes — *_recovered signal
muted In a maintenance window. Signals are recorded but not dispatched. No

How it integrates

SignalForge is designed to plug into your existing on-call toolchain, not replace it. Common patterns:

  • PagerDuty integration — route severity: critical signals to your PagerDuty service key via webhook. PagerDuty handles escalation and on-call rotation.
  • Slack alerts — configure a Slack incoming webhook destination for severity: warning signals to post to your team channel.
  • Custom dashboards — poll GET /v1/signals to populate a Grafana panel or internal status board.
  • CI/CD gating — use the CLI's signalforge status --fail-on-critical flag to block deployments when a critical signal is active.
Team size sweet spot

SignalForge is designed for platform teams of 2–15 engineers who need reliable API monitoring without the overhead of a full observability stack. If you're running a large dedicated SRE team, you may want to evaluate it alongside Datadog or Grafana Cloud.
